title: An unusual Case of p63/p40 Negative Myoepithelial cell-Rich Parotid Pleomorphic Adenoma
html: Pleomorphic adenoma is the most common benign salivary gland neoplasm; however, myoepithelial-rich variants with unusual immunophenotypes are rare and pose diagnostic challenges. We report a myoepithelial-rich pleomorphic adenoma of the parotid gland in a 23-year-old male presenting with a slowly enlarging, painless infraauricular swelling. Grossly, the lesion was well-circumscribed and encapsulated. Histopathology revealed predominantly spindle, oval, and plasmacytoid myoepithelial cells embedded in densely hyalinized fibromyxoid stroma, with sparse ductal structures.
